business.description: Archidply Decor Limited is engaged in manufacturing activities with a focus on improving product quality, optimizing manufacturing processes, and developing environmentally sustainable products and processes. outlook.statement: The Company intends to continue and strengthen its R&D initiatives with a focus on cost optimization, improvement in product quality, enhancement of manufacturing processes and minimization of environmental impact.

The Company remains focused on strengthening its business operations and improving its financial and operational performance. Key focus areas include enhancing capacity utilisation, strengthening plywood and veneer product portfolio, developing value-added product variants, exploring opportunities in engineered wood products (MDF and particle board), improving cost efficiency and operational productivity, strengthening working capital management, expanding relationships with dealers and channel partners, and focusing on product quality, customer service and sustainable business practices.

risks: financial, credit, market, liquidity, security, property, IT, legal, regulatory, reputational and other risks
Fluctuations in the availability and prices of timber, veneer logs, resin and other raw materials may affect the Company's operating margins.
The Company operates in a competitive market and faces competition from domestic manufacturers as well as imported wood-based products.
Changes in environmental regulations, emission standards and certification requirements may increase compliance requirements and operating costs.
Changes in consumer demand, economic conditions, competitive pricing and input costs may put pressure on margins.
Changes in foreign exchange rates may impact the cost of imported raw materials and other imported inputs.
Market risk including foreign currency risk and interest rate risk
Credit risk from trade receivables and financial institutions

qualifications_or_emphasis: I have not examined compliance by the Company with applicable financial laws, like direct and indirect tax laws, since the same have been subject to review by statutory financial audit and other designated professionals.

key_audit_matters: Valuation of Inventories: The Company is having Inventory of Rs. 2,787.17 lakhs as on 31st March, 2026. Inventories are to be valued as per Ind AS 2. Management applies judgment in determining the appropriate provisions against inventory of Stores, Raw Material, Finished goods and Work in progress based upon a detailed analysis of old inventory, net realisable value below cost based upon future plans for sale of inventory.

Revenue recognition on sale of goods and impairment loss allowance on trade receivables: Revenue is measured based on the transaction price, adjusted for volume discounts, rebates, scheme allowances, price concessions, incentives and returns. An estimate of variable consideration payable to the customer is recorded as at the year end. In accordance with Ind AS 109, the Company follows 'simplified approach' for recognition of impairment loss allowance on trade receivables. Management exercises significant judgments and estimates in calculating the said variable consideration and impairment loss allowance.
Verifying for a sample of individual products that costs have been correctly recorded as per Ind AS 2.
Comparing the net realisable value to the cost price of inventories to check for completeness of the associated provision.

Determining the appropriate provisions against inventory of Stores, upon a detailed analysis of old inventory, net realisable value applied to ensure purchased and sold inventory are correctly accounted.
